newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-PIENAAR THE HERO IN TRANSVAAL VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-PIENAAR THE HERO IN TRANSVAAL VICTORY.

text.p: Ousted Springbok captain Francois Pienaar was carried shoulder high from Loftus Versfeld after his team, Transvaal, earned a place in next week's Currie Cup final against Natal by beating Northern Transvaal 31-21 in the semi final (half time 20-6).

An emotional Pienaar, who was not part of the 36 man Springbok squad announced by manager Andre Markgraaff last Saturday, said: "I would like to thank the people of South Africa for supporting me this week. It has been a tough time. Thanks."

Asked if he would be available for the Springbok squad if further injuries occurred, Pienaar left the door open. "That's a tough question to answer at this stage. Obviously I have a contract with SARFU (South African Rugby Football Union) and I must do what they say".

Monday is the deadline for proving fitness for the tour of Argentina, France and Wales and with Os du Randt and Christiaan Scholtz already out of the original squad the possibility of further attrition could bring Pienaar back from the brink.
Transvaal stunned Northerns with three tries in the first 48 minutes.

Fullback Gavin Lawless opened the try scoring with a brilliant score in the right corner and Pienaar was prominent in the movement which saw Springbok centre Japie Mulder force himself over the line for the second.

When another World Cup Springbok Rudolf Straeuli finished a movement which went from one end of the field to the other Transvaal led 25-6 and despite a Northerns revival in the final quarter it was too little too late.
Springbok wing Jaques Olivier gave his side hope by finishing a breakaway try in the 67th minute and repeated infringements led to a 78th minute penalty try.
But Springbok centre Hennie le Roux underlined Transvaal's win gainst the odds with a drop-goal right on full time.
